mistakes: I ran cat through Bash to read defaults.toml. Policy denied it; I then used the Read tool. I should have used Read from the start.
I did not measure the reader-set budget before editing defaults.toml. A single entry of this length would exceed the budget, so I should have checked the margin first.
learnings: defaults.toml entries are all rendered into the reader set by DefaultsModel::render (crates/athena-data/src/defaults.rs), regardless of applies_to. Every new entry therefore counts against the reader budget.

The reader budget test (crates/athena-cli/tests/budgets.rs) uses a 1800-token estimate (ceil(bytes/3.0)). Before this change the reader set was close to full (estimate: about 1798 tokens), so any new default entry of usable length breaks it.
The budget test's failure message says to pay for additions with removals.
desires: A way to see the baseline budget figure without editing files, so I could confirm how much room the reader set had before my change.

A decision on how to pay for the added reader-set tokens: a shorter statement, a removal elsewhere in the reader set, or a budget change. Each of these is outside this job's allowed edits, so I did not make any of them.
